description: Curated analytic chart patterns anchored to pinned Vega-Lite example specs.

items.title: Categorical Comparison
items.analytic_goal: Compare ranked category magnitudes with a simple bar chart.
items.when_to_use: Discrete categories with one main metric and a need for quick ranking.
items.avoid_when: When the x-axis is temporal or when proportions are the primary story.
items.accessibility_notes: Prefer direct labels or accessible tooltips for category-value pairs.
items.description: A simple bar chart with embedded data.

items.title: Trend Over Time
items.analytic_goal: Track a continuous metric across time with a line chart.
items.when_to_use: Time series with enough points to show movement or slope changes.
items.avoid_when: When categories are not ordered in time or there are too many overlapping series.
items.accessibility_notes: Use clear axis titles and point markers when the line is dense.

items.title: Part to Whole
items.analytic_goal: Show a small number of proportions with an arc/pie chart.
items.when_to_use: A handful of categories where percentage share is more important than precision.
items.avoid_when: When there are many slices or subtle percentage differences.
items.accessibility_notes: Provide labels or a fallback table because color alone is weak.
items.description: A simple pie chart with embedded data.

items.title: Binned Density Heatmap
items.analytic_goal: Reveal distribution density across two quantitative axes.
items.when_to_use: Large point clouds where raw scatter marks would overplot heavily.
items.avoid_when: When the audience needs exact point-level values instead of density patterns.
items.accessibility_notes: Pair the color scale with a legend and narrative explanation of density bands.

items.title: Trend With Uncertainty Band
items.analytic_goal: Combine a mean line with confidence intervals in one layered view.
items.when_to_use: Time trends where the uncertainty envelope is as important as the mean.
items.avoid_when: When the audience only needs a point estimate or the intervals are uninterpretable.
items.accessibility_notes: Use a sufficiently opaque band and explain what the interval means.

items.title: Correlation With Group Encoding
items.analytic_goal: Show the relationship between two quantitative fields with grouped points.
items.when_to_use: Pairwise quantitative comparison with categorical grouping.
items.avoid_when: When there are too many points for overlap or no relationship to compare.
items.accessibility_notes: Use both color and shape so groups remain distinguishable.
items.description: A scatterplot showing body mass and flipper lengths of penguins.

items.title: Small Multiples Comparison
items.analytic_goal: Use faceting to compare repeated measures across categories.
items.when_to_use: One repeated structure per site, region, or cohort needs side-by-side reading.
items.avoid_when: When there are too many facets or the repeated pattern is not comparable.
items.accessibility_notes: Keep facet counts manageable and titles descriptive.
items.description: The Trellis display by Becker et al. helped establish small multiples as a “powerful mechanism for understanding interactions in studies of how a response depends on explanatory variables”. Here we reproduce a trellis of Barley yields from the 1930s, complete with main-effects ordering to facilitate comparison.

items.title: Scatterplot Matrix
items.analytic_goal: Inspect many pairwise quantitative relationships at once.
items.when_to_use: Several quantitative measures need broad exploratory comparison.
items.avoid_when: When the audience only needs one or two key relationships.
items.accessibility_notes: Highlight the most important pairs in narrative text for faster reading.
